finding: src/anomaly/workflow.py:109 Invocation-wide gate decisions can bypass both required human turn boundaries.
rationale: No upstream stage-aware guard exists: the public entry accepts Gate A and Gate B together, retains both decisions for the whole invocation, checks only key presence at P4/P7, and continues after successful P3/P6 seals, so both required paused returns are reachable to bypass.

evidence.output: run_workflow calls normalize_inputs once into supplied before entering while True; every iteration builds available from that same supplied mapping, pauses only when resolution.status == 'paused', otherwise executes the owner, and continues unless the phase becomes blocked or unavailable.

_REQUIRED_INPUTS maps P4 to gate_a and P7 to gate_b; _missing_input returns no pause whenever the name is present. normalize_inputs accepts both names in _PUBLIC_INPUTS, copies the whole caller mapping, and has no phase-aware rejection or deferral guard.

The P4 handler reads inputs['gate_a'] and immediately approves/detects; P7 reads inputs['gate_b'] and immediately accepts/reports. A successful non-P7 phase is sealed with status 'active', so after P3 and P6 run_workflow loops directly to the next ready owner instead of returning a human-turn pause.
The locked acceptance criterion requires Gate A/Gate B turn boundaries, and task state records the inspected candidate as clean and green at gated hash 4a1746f9050120df52e7845166f0ab935c4e584a.
